findings.problem: Comment proposes Rayon for a [u8; 4] input. Rayon task-creation, work-stealing, and sync overhead dwarfs any benefit on four elements. No benchmark, baseline, or hardware target exists.
findings.failure_mode: Adding Rayon on four elements will measurably slow the hot path due to thread-pool dispatch overhead, producing a regression on every call.
findings.fix: Remove the Rayon proposal. For four elements, a direct iterator chain (current code) is already the fastest measured option. If zero-allocation is required, return [u8; 4] of tag bytes instead of Vec<&str>.

findings.problem: Comment proposes SmallVec for a [u8; 4] input producing exactly four elements. SmallVec's inline capacity and layout overhead bloats the return type with no heap-savings benefit on known-four elements.
findings.failure_mode: SmallVec<&'static str; N> with N>=4 heap-allocates on a four-element input just like Vec, adding layout indirection and a capacity check for zero benefit.
findings.fix: Replace Vec<&'static str> with [u8; 4] of inline tag bytes (e.g., 0 = even, 1 = odd) or a [u32; 4] packed bitfield. This eliminates all allocation and is cache-friendly.

findings.problem: Returns Vec<&'static str> for a fixed four-element input. Every call heap-allocates a new Vec, which is unnecessary for a known-bound size.
findings.failure_mode: Every invocation performs a heap allocation and deallocation. Under sustained call rate this generates GC pressure (on FFI boundaries), allocator contention, and tail-latency spikes.
findings.fix: Return [u8; 4] of inline even/odd tags, or accept a caller-owned output buffer: fn classify_four(bytes: &[u8; 4], out: &mut [u8; 4]). This gives zero-allocation performance with static bounds.

findings.problem: No benchmark, no baseline number, no workload definition, no target hardware. The comment claims Rayon+SmallVec 'will be faster' without any measurement.
findings.failure_mode: Performance claims without evidence are folklore. Deploying folklore changes as optimization regresses throughput and latency on all realistic workloads.
findings.fix: Delete the unmeasured claim. Run cargo bench with a realistic workload before proposing any change. For [u8; 4] the baseline is already near optimal.

findings.problem: Function signature returns Vec, forcing allocation on every call. The domain is four independent even/odd tags with no variable length.
findings.failure_mode: Caller cannot reuse output storage. Allocator fragmentation under repeated calls. Impossible to use in allocation-free hot paths or embedded contexts.
findings.fix: Change signature to fn classify_four(bytes: &[u8; 4]) -> [u8; 4] encoding even as 0 and odd as 1, or fn classify_four(bytes: &[u8; 4], out: &mut [u8; 4]) -> Result<(), ()>.

findings.problem: No benches/ directory or benchmark crate exists. No profiler output, no allocation counts, no command evidence for any performance claim.
findings.failure_mode: Without benchmarks the codebase cannot validate that any change improves performance. Folklore-driven changes silently regress.
findings.fix: Add a benches/ crate with criterion or similar. Benchmark classify_four with representative byte distributions at realistic call rates. Report ops/sec with p50/p95/p99 and allocation counts.

no profiler output (flamegraph, perf record, or equivalent)
no allocation analysis (Rustc -Z sanitisers, valgrind, or malloc_count)
no second-ring evidence (assembly diff, LLVM IR, or cache-line analysis)

no baseline measurement to compare any proposed change against
residual_risk: Static review only. No commands ran. The code compiles and is structurally correct for its domain, but returns Vec for fixed-four input and carries an unmeasured folklore performance claim. The function is safe and deterministic. Risk is moderate: no correctness or safety violations, but the signature forces allocation and the TODO comment encourages folklore-driven changes that will regress performance if followed.
